Verdict: REVISEThe note contains a sound conditional two-partition calculation and a valid donor-incidence bookkeeping principle, but the main closed-cavity theorem is not established under the hypotheses as written. The decisive missing ingredients are:a closure condition quantified over every endpoint component meeting the cavity, including unlisted or incomplete components;an explicit proof that the deleted extreme columns contain no endpoints and exactly  $2h$  selected supports;a one-square/support-clearance condition ensuring that every shifted receiver is actually present and has the claimed labels;an exact parity condition for every enclosed source relative to both the original and shifted tilings;a phase-preserving definition of the up/down reflection;a universal symbolic interface proof for the nested  $a$ -source construction.There are also two statements that are actually false under their literal wording:the universal shifted charge claim  $E'_C=-n$  for arbitrary relative placements and vertical reflections;the statement that the explicit occupied-rung example “refutes the sufficiency” of the old endpoint-free-rung criterion.The latter example may refute necessity or completeness of that criterion, depending on its exact formulation, but an example that fails a sufficient hypothesis cannot refute the hypothesis’s sufficiency.1. What is correct conditionallyLet
$$N=\frac{(h+1)(w-2)}2,\qquad
N'=\frac{(h+1)(w-4)}2.$$
Thus  $N-N'=h+1$ . Let  $t$  and  $p$  be the total selected and endpoint counts in  $C$ , and let
$$E_C=\sum_{\substack{Q\subset C\\Q\cap P\neq\varnothing}}
\left(t_Q+\frac{p_Q}{2}-2\right)$$
be the raw excess over endpoint-containing original tiles. If the shifted partition removes exactly  $2h$  selected boundary supports and no endpoints, then
$$D_C
 =2N-t-\frac p2+E_C,$$
and
$$D'_C
 =2N'-(t-2h)-\frac p2+E'_C.$$
Therefore
$$D_C-D'_C
 =2(N-N')-2h+E_C-E'_C
 =2+E_C-E'_C. \tag{A}$$
This algebra is correct. Also, once the shifted squares really are feasible  $2\times2$  squares, the local bound  $t_Q\le 2$  gives  $D'_C\ge 0$ .Consequently, the claimed identity
$$D_C=2+2n+D'_C$$
would follow if, and only if, the following two raw-excess statements have been established:
$$E_C=n,\qquad E'_C=-n. \tag{B}$$
The first is conditional on the original source and comb receiver calculations. The second is the difficult new assertion. It does not follow merely from the given original charge  $+1$ .2. Complete-component containment does not by itself give receiver containmentThe note says that component closure and absence of boundary endpoints imply that every enclosed receiver is present in both partitions. This needs to be separated into two claims.2.1 Endpoint-component containment is not the same as receiver containmentThe condition
$$P\text{-component }H\subseteq C$$
only says that the endpoint vertices lie in  $C$ . It does not automatically say that:every aligned endpoint-containing tile lies in  $C$ ;every shifted endpoint-containing square lies in  $C$ ;all prescribed supports affecting the raw count lie in  $C$ ;no endpoint lies in the two extreme columns deleted by the shifted partition.In particular, an endpoint component can be wholly contained in  $C$  while an endpoint lies in one of the deleted side columns. Its endpoint-containing aligned square can then be present in the original partition but absent from the shifted partition. The implication
$$\text{component contained in }C
\Longrightarrow
\text{all shifted endpoint squares contained in }C$$
is false in general.For the particular root geometry, the desired boundary exclusion appears derivable, but it is not stated as an assumption and is not proved in the note.2.2 The required boundary lemma is plausible but missingAt the left extreme column  $x=1$ , the fixed root source gives selected inward supports at rows
$$3,5,\ldots,r-1,$$
exactly  $h$  sites. The same holds at  $x=w-2$ , so the claimed total  $2h$  is correct provided that all other boundary sites are forced blank.A complete proof should handle the following cases explicitly.At rows  $q=2,4,\ldots,r$ , a candidate  $T$ -vertex at  $(q,1)$  is adjacent to the root arm endpoint  $(q,0)$  and to the retained inward support at  $(q-1,1)$ . It would therefore have two occupied neighbors and is infeasible.A candidate  $P$ -vertex at  $(q,1)$  for  $q\le r$  is adjacent to the root arm endpoint  $(q,0)$ , so it would either extend the root endpoint component across the boundary or create a component that violates the intended closure condition.At row  $r+1$ , the retained axial support  $(r+1,0)$  already sees the root tip  $(r,0)$ . Any  $T$ - or  $P$ -vertex at  $(r+1,1)$  would give that support a second occupied neighbor.The mirror argument applies at  $x=w-2$ .Thus the exact count  $2h$  is recoverable from the root geometry, but the current sentence “every other site is blank” is a proof gap. If “every complete endpoint component” does not quantify over all endpoint components, including unlisted or incomplete ones, then it is more serious: an unlisted component could put an endpoint on the boundary, and both the  $2h$  count and equation (A) would fail.The note itself later says that “an arbitrary unprescribed component crossing  $C$  is not covered.” That admission is incompatible with using  $E_C=n$  and  $E'_C=-n$  for the entire cavity unless the closure hypothesis is strengthened to exclude every such component.A correct hypothesis would be something like:Every endpoint component meeting  $C$  is one of the listed root-enclosed sources or complete combs, is wholly contained in the interior of  $C$ , and no endpoint occurs in the deleted boundary columns.That condition must include unlisted components, not just the prescribed ones.3. The shifted source charge  $-1$  is not universal as writtenThis is the principal mathematical problem.The original prescribed source charge  $+1$  is computed in one fixed physical tiling. The shifted raw excess is computed in a different partition. Changing the partition changes:the number of endpoint-containing squares;which supports are inside the receiver;whether a chamber end or arm tip is split;whether an axial support is in the last receiver square;which corners are forced blank.There is no general principle that carries the original charge  $+1$  to a shifted charge  $-1$ .3.1 One-column translation gives an explicit phase counterexampleUsing the source-template coordinates for  $w=8$ ,  $h=1$ , consider the positive down-opening source phase. The source has
$$|P|=22.$$
In the phase for which the original receiver has the template count
$$|R|=9,\qquad T_R=8,$$
the original raw charge is
$$E=T_R+\frac{|P|}{2}-2|R|
 =8+11-18
 =1.$$
For the horizontally shifted partition, the same source has
$$|R'|=8,\qquad T_{R'}=4,$$
so
$$E'=4+11-16=-1.$$
That is the phase claimed in the note.Now translate the entire source by one horizontal vertex while retaining the same matching, supports, and relative geometry. In a sufficiently wide cavity this remains a feasible translated source. The two tilings exchange roles:
$$|R|=8,\qquad T_R=4,$$
and hence
$$E=4+11-16=-1,$$
while
$$|R'|=9,\qquad T_{R'}=8,$$
so
$$E'=8+11-18=+1.$$
Therefore the pair
$$(E,E')=(+1,-1)$$
is not valid for arbitrary feasible relative placements. The translated source gives
$$(E,E')=(-1,+1).$$
If “positive physical alignment” is intended to prohibit this translation, then the note must define that alignment as an exact parity condition relative to both tilings. The phrase is currently too informal to carry the quantifier “arbitrary relative positions subject to feasibility.”3.2 Literal vertical reflection also changes the shifted chargeThe assertion that vertical reflection preserves the shifted counts is likewise false unless the reflection is required to preserve the row phase of the fixed tiling.For the same  $w=8,h=1$  source, take the intended down-opening placement and reflect it literally by
$$y\longmapsto 4-y$$
without a compensating translation. The chamber moves to rows  $3,4$ , and the arms occupy rows  $0,1,2$ . Keeping the shifted row pairing fixed at
$$(0,1),(2,3),(4,5),\ldots,$$
the shifted endpoint receiver has
$$|R'|=10,\qquad T_{R'}=2,\qquad |P|=22.$$
Hence
$$E'=2+11-20=-7,$$
not  $-1$ .The exact value is less important than the mechanism: a reflection whose coordinate sum has the wrong parity does not preserve a fixed tiling. It changes which chamber and arm rows share receiver squares and moves the axial and lateral supports in or out of the receiver.A valid theorem must require one of the following:a reflection that preserves the row phase of both partitions; ora reflection followed by a prescribed phase-restoring translation; ora separate raw-count calculation for the up-opening orientation.The current wording “may open up or down” and “reflecting vertically preserves these counts” is insufficient.3.3 “Arbitrary retaining feasible completions” is also unprovedEven with the correct source parity, the established freezing lemma freezes the prescribed endpoint component and fixes labels in the original receiver. It does not automatically fix every label in every shifted square.The shifted receiver may contain corners that are not part of the original receiver. To conclude that  $E'$  is invariant under arbitrary feasible completions, one needs a separate shifted-receiver rigidity lemma proving that every site contributing to the shifted endpoint squares is forced to be:the prescribed  $P$ -vertex;the prescribed support  $T$ -vertex; orblank.The sentence“All relevant receiver labels are fixed in arbitrary feasible completions retaining the prescribed data”is currently an assertion, not a consequence of the granted source freezing result.The axial-support argument must also be made inside the cavity. A source endpoint path can be contained in  $C$  while its axial support lies outside  $C$ . Component containment alone does not give the one-row support clearance needed for the asserted shifted tip count.3.4 The correct repairFor each enclosed source, require and prove:fixed horizontal parity relative to the original and shifted column phases;fixed vertical parity relative to the row tiling;a one-square or one-row clearance from every cavity boundary relevant to the shifted receiver;inclusion of the complete prescribed support envelope, not merely the  $P$ -component, in the cavity;a shifted-receiver label-forcing lemma;a separate proof for the phase-preserving up-opening orientation.Under those strengthened conditions, the contribution
$$E=+1,\qquad E'=-1$$
may be correct. It is not correct for the current unrestricted placement statement.4. Complete combs and  $D'_C$ The complete-comb part is substantially better supported.Given the granted complete-comb theorem in every alignment, a complete straight comb has whole raw sum zero in either partition, provided its entire endpoint receiver is present. The shifted partition does not introduce a problem by itself if:no comb endpoint lies in the deleted extreme columns;no endpoint receiver is clipped by the cavity boundary;the shifted complete receiver is actually the whole receiver used in the comb theorem.Likewise,  $D'_C\ge 0$  follows from the local two-selection bound on each shifted square.Thus the comb contribution is conditionally acceptable. It does not repair the source-phase and closure problems.5. Donor multiplicity and overlap allocationThe donor-incidence argument in Section 3 is valid once the individual cavity identities are valid.If
$$D_C=\sum_{Q\in C\text{ no-endpoint}}(2-t_Q)$$
and every positive-deficit physical tile belongs to at most  $c$  cavities, then
$$\sum_j D_{C_j}\le cD_{\mathrm{all}}.$$
Combining this with  $D_{C_j}\ge 2k_j$  gives
$$2K\le \sum_jD_{C_j}\le cD_{\mathrm{all}},$$
and therefore
$$c\Delta
 =c(D_{\mathrm{all}}-B+E)
 \ge 2K-cB+cE.$$
No physical donor is reused beyond the declared multiplicity. The weighted version is also correct: if
$$\sum_{j:Q\in C_j}\lambda_j\le 1$$
for every positive donor  $Q$ , then
$$\sum_j\lambda_jD_{C_j}\le D_{\mathrm{all}}.$$
This part does not infer allocation from source counts alone. It correctly distinguishes source coverage from physical donor capacity.The limitation is that this argument is only as strong as the individual  $D_{C_j}\ge 2k_j$  identities. If a cavity contains an unlisted component, a clipped receiver, or a source with the wrong phase, the incidence calculation cannot fix the failure.6. Normalization preservationThe normalization paragraph is acceptable only conditionally on the precise normalization theorem.If the granted normalization result really guarantees that:all prescribed source and comb endpoints remain frozen;no new endpoint is created in  $C$ ;no endpoint component is extended across the cavity boundary;selected supports and matching transfers used in the cavity proof remain unchanged;then normalization does not cause donor reuse. The donors remain physical tiles, and the incidence inequality continues to count each one by its actual multiplicity.The current note only says:“Normalization only promotes existing endpoints; it never adds endpoints.”That is not enough unless “existing endpoints” is a formally established invariant of the normalization operation. If normalization can change  $P$ , matching edges, or the labels of no-endpoint tiles, then the two-partition hypotheses must be rechecked after normalization. The note should invoke the exact normalization-preservation statement rather than relying on this informal summary.7. The explicit zero-mouth familyThe explicit construction appears to accomplish a useful, but narrower, purpose.7.1 What the construction does establishFor the displayed pattern, the geometry is plausible and internally consistent: $L$  and  $R$  are the only two parallel negative combs in the prescribed pattern; $H$  is a complete horizontal comb with zero whole charge;the upper saturated-tip rung between  $L$  and  $R$ ,
$$\{6,7\}\times\{10,\ldots,21\},$$
contains the endpoints of  $H$ ;therefore that particular saturated-tip rung is not endpoint-free;the cavity compensation calculation gives  $D_C=2+D'_C\ge2$  for the root-only case, hence  $\Delta\ge1$ .So the example does not contradict the coefficient-one target. It exhibits a configuration where the old saturated-tip route is unavailable while a separate cavity deficit supplies compensation.7.2 The lower mouth strip must be discussed explicitlyThe lower strip between the vertical combs is different. It is in the source mouth, and the vertical comb ends there are sparse rather than saturated. In the shown pattern, the lower corridor is endpoint-free away from the two comb boundary columns.Therefore the family blocks the useful saturated-tip upper rung, but it does not necessarily block every possible “endpoint-free rung” if the old criterion permits a rung at either tip or permits a sparse-tip pairing.The note must state the old criterion exactly. There are two possibilities:If the criterion specifically requires the saturated remote tip, then the construction blocks that criterion’s hypothesis.If the criterion merely requires some endpoint-free rung between the two combs, the construction may not block it, because the lower mouth strip can still be endpoint-free.The phrase “the only possible endpoint-free remote rung pair” is therefore too broad. It should read something like:“The only saturated-tip rung available to the prescribed negative-comb pair is occupied by the horizontal comb.”7.3 The sufficiency sentence is logically wrongThe note says:“This refutes the sufficiency of the existing endpoint-free pair criterion for this family.”That conclusion does not follow. A sufficient criterion has the form
$$\text{criterion}\Longrightarrow\text{desired conclusion}.$$
An example that fails the criterion says nothing against that implication. The construction could show:the criterion is not necessary;the criterion is not complete as a coverage strategy;there are valid configurations outside the criterion’s domain.It would refute sufficiency only if the example satisfied the criterion but failed the conclusion.This is an actual false statement, independent of the other proof gaps.8. The all- $a$  nested familyI found no immediate local geometric contradiction in the coordinate pattern itself.For source  $i$ :the arms are at columns  $3+8i$  and  $w+2-8i$ ;the two associated vertical combs are three columns away;the horizontal comb is four columns from the associated vertical comb paths;neighboring source chambers are separated by eight rows;the common tip row is  $y=2h+4$ ;the stated even-width and depth formulas keep all matching paths of the required parity.The asserted interface margins are therefore plausible under the supplied source and comb freezing lemmas.However, the universal proof is incomplete. The following must be proved symbolically for every  $a$ , even  $e$ , and  $d\ge0$ :every selected support has exactly its intended occupied neighbor;no support is adjacent to a second endpoint or to another selected support;no two endpoint components share a physical tile;no matching edge crosses between source and comb receivers;all source and comb supports remain inside the intended terminal rectangle;every nonroot component is contained in the root cavity;the common source phase gives the claimed pair  $(E,E')=(+1,-1)$  for every nested source;the normalization-preservation statement continues to hold simultaneously for all  $a$  sources and  $3a$  combs.The prose about “three-column gaps,” “four-column gaps,” and “closest cross-row supports” is a good outline, but it is not yet an all- $a$  proof. The finite controls with counts up to  $a=5$  are useful evidence and may catch coordinate mistakes, but they do not establish the universal quantifier.Thus the nested family should be marked plausible construction, proof incomplete, rather than accepted as a proved all-count theorem.9. Status of the requested questionsQuestionReview resultDoes complete-component containment include all endpoint squares in both partitions?No, not by itself. It must be supplemented by endpoint-free deleted boundary strips and support/receiver clearance.Is the boundary selection count exactly  $2h$ ?Yes for the displayed root geometry after a missing boundary case proof; not established from the present closure wording alone.Is a parallel positive source’s shifted raw charge always  $-1$ ?No under literal arbitrary relative placements or phase-changing reflection. It is conditional on an explicit parity and phase-preserving hypothesis.Do donor multiplicity claims avoid reuse?Yes, conditionally. The incidence inequality is mathematically sound.Do normalization claims avoid reuse?Only if the granted normalization theorem really preserves the endpoint/support/receiver data. The note should state that theorem precisely.Does the zero-mouth family block the only possible endpoint-free remote rung?It blocks the upper saturated-tip rung in the displayed pattern. It does not automatically block every rung notion; the lower sparse mouth corridor must be excluded by definition or analysis.Does the zero-mouth family contradict the target?No. Its cavity deficit gives  $\Delta\ge1$  in the root-only case.Is the all- $a$  nested interface proof valid?No as a written universal proof yet. The geometry appears plausible, but the all-count contact and phase arguments remain to be supplied.Required revisions for an ACCEPTable theoremThe note would become substantially stronger if Section 1 were replaced by an explicit strengthened hypothesis containing:all-component closure: every endpoint component meeting  $C$ , including unprescribed components, is one of the listed source or comb components and is contained in  $C$ ;deleted-boundary exclusion: no endpoint occurs in the two extreme columns used by the shifted partition;boundary-support lemma: a proof of the exact  $2h$  selected count;source-envelope containment: every axial, lateral, and blank-forcing support used in the shifted count lies in the cavity or is explicitly accounted for;fixed phase: exact row and column parity relative to both tilings;phase-preserving reflection: up/down orientation is defined with the necessary parity-restoring translation;shifted-receiver rigidity: a proof that arbitrary retaining feasible completions cannot change any shifted receiver label;precise rung definition: distinguish “any endpoint-free rung” from “the saturated-tip remote rung”;all- $a$  interface lemma: a finite symbolic case table covering source-source, source-comb, comb-comb, and support-support contacts for arbitrary  $a,e,d$ .With those additions, equation (A), the donor-incidence argument, and the explicit constructions could support a rigorous conditional compensation theorem. In its present form, the correct review result is REVISE.
